newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says missiles smashed Iraq defenses.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says missiles smashed Iraq defenses.

text.p: U.S. cruise missiles severely degraded Iraqi anti-aircraft defences, destroying or damaging up to 11 of 15 targets, the Pentagon said on Friday in its first public assessment of raids on southern Iraq.

"The overall assessment was that the two strikes ... achieved a severe degradation of Iraq defences south of the 33rd parallel," Defence Department spokesman Ken Bacon said of the 44 missiles fired by U.S. warships and bombers on Monday and Tuesday.

The satellite-guided missiles were fired from more than 500 miles (800 km) away in two waves against air defence targets in southern Iraq to punish Saddam for a military drive into a Western-protected safe haven for Kurds in northern Iraq.

Stressing that the damage assessment was not complete, Bacon told reporters the Tomahawk ship-launched missiles and cruise missiles fired by B-52 bombers were aimed at eight surface-to-air (SAM) missile sites and seven air defence command and control facilities.

He said five of the eight SAM sites were "severely damaged or destroyed" and at least one other damaged or vacated. One command site was destroyed or severely damaged and four others were damaged, vacated or degraded, he added.
"What we had is a mission that succeeded in its goal which was suppressing enemy air defences," he told reporters in response to questions.

Bacon said the final results of the strikes had not been determined by U.S. intelligence but that the missiles, designed to land within a 12-meter radius circle from well over 500 miles (800 km) away at least half of the time, had apparently performed well.

"We are not flawless and the weapons do not meet their specifications 100 percent of the time," said Bacon, adding that two anti-aircraft missile launchers had been moved before the attack and two command sites received only minor or no damage at all.

He said that damage assessment was a very difficult task because some targets were more "hardened" with concrete than others and that missiles needed to hit such hardened targets with pinpoint accuracy in order to destroy them completely.
